leftEvidence.role: Famine, Song, Last Words, and Census
leftEvidence.title: Last words join spirit, rule, and covenant

points.label: Action and response
points.left: David identifies himself through ancestry, anointing, song, and divine speech; just rule is compared to morning light and an everlasting covenant is named beside worthless thorns.
points.right: The warriors’ names and acts move from three champions to a larger company, including the water brought from Bethlehem and ending with Uriah the Hittite.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places the last-word frame holds ideal rule beside David’s own house and hope inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places heroic memory ends by naming Uriah inside David’s company inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: 2 Samuel 23:1–7 and 2 Samuel 23:8–39 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Famine, Song, Last Words, and Census” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.

rightEvidence.role: Famine, Song, Last Words, and Census
rightEvidence.title: Mighty deeds and named companions surround the king

payload.tension: 2 Samuel 23:1–7 foregrounds the last-word frame holds ideal rule beside David’s own house and hope; 2 Samuel 23:8–39 foregrounds heroic memory ends by naming Uriah inside David’s company. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
